commits.message:
docs(style): drop the panel title from the styles that degrade

A Panel reads its title as plain text, so a style on it is never resolved
and never reaches onStyleError. The sentence now names only a table cell,
which does degrade and report. The title bug is rich-panel ticket filed
separately.

docs(style): document the degrade-versus-strict contract (rich-diagnostics-un7.5)

docs/style.md never said that an invalid style inside text is dropped
silently, so a reader whose text printed plain had nothing to go on. The
new "When a style is invalid" section says what degrades (styles attached
to text: markup tags, RichText styles, spans, highlighters) and what throws
StyleSyntaxError (Style.parse, new Theme, print/Console style options, a
renderable's own border/rule/guide styles), links markup parse errors to
docs/markup.md, and covers onStyleError, including the did-you-mean message
and per-resolution call counts, and rethrowing from it as the strict mode.

docs/markup.md's parse-errors section now points a misspelled style name
at that section, since it is not a parse error.

Every behavioral claim and the sample message were checked against real
output. renderToString has no handler; that gap is filed as
rich-diagnostics-ejn.

feat(markup): report where a markup string fails to parse (rich-diagnostics-un7.4) (#140)

* feat(markup): report where a markup string fails to parse (rich-diagnostics-un7.4)

A markup parse failure now throws MarkupSyntaxError, a subclass of
MarkupError. The message gives the line and column of the rejected tag,
an excerpt of that line with a caret under the tag, and the tags still
open there. The same facts are fields (reason, markup, offset, line,
column, openTags) for callers building their own message.

It is a subclass rather than optional fields because MarkupRegistry.register
also throws MarkupError and has no source text to point into. Existing
catches of MarkupError still catch parse failures.

The plugin-aware walk parses the caller's string in slices, so every
parse now carries its origin: the whole string, where the slice starts
in it, and the plugin tags around it. Offsets are reported in the
caller's string at any depth.

The excerpt is cut to 30 code points either side, places the caret by
cell width, and shows control characters as spaces so the caret stays
aligned and the message cannot emit terminal escapes.

The rich-explore coverage demo previously used "[bold[bad", which never
threw, so its MarkupError line never printed; it now fails for real and
shows the location.

* fix(markup): keep control characters out of every part of the error message

Review of #140 found two problems.

The excerpt replaced control characters with spaces, but the reason and
the "Open tags" line quoted tag text raw. The tag grammar admits ESC, so
"[bold\x1b]" put ESC ] (the start of an OSC sequence) into a message meant
for a terminal. printable() is now the one rule every quoted part of the
message goes through. The reason and openTags fields keep the text as
written.

Inside a plugin tag, "[aa][/][/aa]" said "[/] has nothing to close" and
then listed [aa] as open. [/] never closes a plugin tag, so the reason
now says there is no open style tag, which is true in both cases.

* fix(markup): name every plugin pair open where an overlap is rejected

Medium review of #140: the overlap error's openTags was [outer, inner],
picked by hand, so a third pair still open at the caret was left out.
In "[pa][pb][pc][/pa][/pc][/pb]" it named [pa] [pb] and not [pc]. It is now
derived from the pairs themselves: a pair is open at the caret when it
opens before the rejected closing tag and closes at or after it.

The review's other finding, that "[bold]x[click]y[/click]z[/bold]" reports
no open tags, comes from style tags not spanning a plugin pair at all,
which master already rejects. It is filed as rich-markup-cg6 rather than
reworded here.
